title: A helper file is named by its record: the code standard counts it as the record's file for R05 and R01, and not for R02
when: Reads a spec built for the test whose helper_file table names helper files of a predicate record, one in the package of the record's file and one in a package that a record of another domain names, through ReadSpec. Then it runs assure.fileWithoutRecord, assure.packageOfTwoDomains and assure.identifierMissing over a tree built for it. Then it reads the same spec without the helper_file table and runs the checks again.
then: Expects a helper file not to be found as a source file without a record, and a file that no record names, or that only a row for an unknown record names, to be found. Expects the title of the record to be checked only against the record's own file, so an identifier that only the helper file declares is found missing. title: Each whole service declaration in a user doc passes stego validate against the repository's registry
when: Reads each doc that the user doc inventory lists, and writes each fenced YAML block whose first line is kind: service as the service.yaml of a new project in a Git repository, with the doc's zed block at the declared schema path and the doc's proto block at each path of the setting proto_files of the component command; runs the stego binary's fill create with the slot command.command, query.query or worker.worker for each fill that a command, a query or a worker names, as the fill workflow of docs/commands-queries-workers.md gives it; then runs the stego binary's validate there. Each run has STEGO_REGISTRY set to the repository's registry. When fill create wrote fills, stego test runs and stego fill sign signs each fill with listed-ssh of ST-EXT-TD02, a key that the test run makes, before stego validate (ST-GEN-INV10).
then: Expects each stego fill create and stego validate to exit 0 for each block, and at least one such block, as README.md's quick start holds one.

title: Each excerpt block of a user doc is whole lines of a checked block of the same doc
when: Reads each doc that the user doc inventory lists, takes each fenced block at any indentation without the indentation of its fence, and counts the lines <!-- excerpt -->. A block that such a line comes just before is an excerpt. In docs/commands-queries-workers.md, and in each doc that holds a marker, it also takes each yaml, zed and proto block that is not an excerpt.
then: Expects each excerpt to be not empty and a run of whole lines of a checked block of the same doc: a whole service declaration for yaml, and the first zed or proto block, which ST-STD-DOCS-R02-T02 writes into the project, for zed and proto; each marker line to come just before a fence; and, in those docs, each other yaml block to be a whole service declaration or a fill manifest that the strict fill.yaml decoder reads and whose fill and slot a command, a query or a worker of the declaration binds, and no second zed or proto block. Each failure names the doc and the line of the block.
notes: A part of a declaration that a doc shows is checked through the whole declaration that it comes from, which ST-STD-DOCS-R02-T02 validates. Added for the user doc of commands, queries and workers (walkthrough-5 D1, 2026-11-16); made strict after the review of PR #396 (M3). The other docs on the inventory still hold unmarked parts of declarations (README.md, docs/schema-changes.md); see followups.md.

notes: With the flag -update-docs, the test first writes each generated section again in the working tree, from the working tree's spec, and logs each doc it wrote, to commit before the next run.

title: A change that alters or removes a CLI command a user doc names, and leaves the doc as it is, gives a reason; one that changes the doc gives none
when: Runs the check that the change gate runs (assure.docsLagChange) on a base whose README names one stego command in its prose and another only in a generated section, for a change that alters the descriptions of both, for one that removes the first, for one that also changes the README, and for one that alters no command.
then: Expects one reason for the altered command named in prose, which reads back as a fault of ST-STD-DOCS-R04 keyed by the command's record; one reason for the removed command; and no reason for the change that changes the README or for the change that alters no command.

title: No generator source imports a package for files, processes or the network, or calls an HTTP client or server
when: Parses every non-test Go file under internal/generator, and lists each import and each package-qualified name, through any import alias.
then: Expects no import of os, os/exec, os/signal, io/ioutil, syscall, net or plugin, and no use of an HTTP client, transport, server or file server.
notes: The generators use net/http only to check route patterns on an in-memory ServeMux, and net/url and net/textproto only to parse text, so those packages stay allowed.

title: No generator source reads the clock, a timer, the environment or a source of randomness
when: Parses every non-test Go file under internal/generator, as ST-STD-GEN-R01-T01 does.
then: Expects no use of time.Now, timers, context deadlines, os.Getenv and its kin, math/rand or crypto/rand. The test can list a known violation, and fails when a listed use is gone; the list is empty.
notes: The gRPC generator stopped proto compilation after 10 seconds until 2026-10-28. The timeout was removed, because the compiler's input size limits already bound the proto files.

title: Planning each built-in archetype ten times gives the same files in the same order
when: With a project for each built-in archetype: rest-crud, rpc-service and browser-service: Plans each project ten times in one process. Go starts each map iteration at a random place.
then: Expects every plan of a project to hold the same files, in the same order, with the same content.
notes: Not proof yet. The three archetypes reach 10 of the 26 components. These are not reached: cli-application, controller, go-sdk, grpc-application, http-application, kafka-producer, keycloak-provider, kubernetes-client, kubernetes-workload, outbox, postgres-client, rh-sso-auth, runtime-configuration, typescript-sdk, user-management and user-management-rhsso. A project for each of them, or a fixture context per generator, would make the test proof.

title: The TLS open files that the compiler emits are as gofmt formats them
when: Formats each file of httpTLSFiles, the unix and the other build-tag variant of the open of a TLS file, with go/format.
then: Expects each to parse and to be byte for byte the same after the formatting.
notes: Follow-up of fu-36 (2026-11-13): http_tls_open_unix.go and http_tls_open_other.go were emitted on one line each. Mutation caught: the old one-line text.

title: Every generated Go file of the examples is as gofmt formats it
when: Reads every Go file under an out folder of the examples and formats it with go/format.
then: Expects at least one file, and each file to be byte for byte the same after the formatting.
notes: The examples are regenerated from a clean clone in CI, so this test sees what the generators emit. It failed before the examples were regenerated with the formatted TLS files.

title: Every suite gives the same outcome on a workstation as in CI at one commit
when: Runs each suite command of the documented list on a developer's workstation, as an unprivileged user, in a network namespace whose only routes are loopback and the network of the local services that the suite starts, with KUBECONFIG unset, no kube configuration file, and no CI provider token, registry credential or cloud credential in the environment, at the commit under test, and reads the outcomes by test ID.
then: Expects each test ID that proves an obligation to have an outcome, and the same result (passed, failed or skipped) as the CI run of the same commit. Expects no test to be skipped or to fail because a cluster, a hosted service, a credential or a route out is missing, and names each test that is.
notes: Not automated yet. Product-wide: it runs every suite at once, so a suite that no domain owns, such as scripts or the Python suites, is also caught; the tests of ST-PAT-LOCAL-TEST-R01 run the same check one domain at a time. A missing outcome is a fault, not a pass. Compare with the CI outcomes of the same commit, so that a test that fails for its own assertion does not count against this rule.

title: No automated test of the product needs a privileged container, a cluster or a hosted credential
when: Reads each file that an automated test record of the product names, and scans its code lines for a privileged container, a container in a namespace of the host, an added capability or device, a read of a kube configuration or of a credential of a hosted service, and a run of kubectl, oc, helm, argocd, gh or kind.
then: Expects each named file to be in the tree, and none of these in any of them. Names each file and line that has one.
notes: Product-wide: it runs the checks of the tests of ST-PAT-LOCAL-TEST on every automated test record of the product at once, also those that sit under no domain, such as the tests of a shared generator library. It reads the records in the pinned lathe check --json and the files they name at HEAD, before any run. A line that compiles a regular expression is not read, so a check can name the text that it looks for. ST-STD-LOCAL-R0x-T01, which runs every suite, stays the product-wide run.

title: A check that turns TLS on in the local PostgreSQL server is built before it takes the TLS lock and runs under it
when: Gives runTLSCheck, which the four checks that turn TLS on in the local PostgreSQL server call, a module in a temporary folder with one test package, and reads with TryLock whether the TLS lock is held after the build of the check and at its run.
then: Expects the check to run and pass in its package folder, the lock to be free after the build and held at the run, and the lock to be free after the check.
notes: Follow-up of the security review of PR #507, I1: runTLSCheck held the lock during go test, so the compile of each inner check waited for the check before it. Mutation caught: the lock taken before go test -c.

title: The checks of R01 find a privileged container in a shell script, a cluster client held in a name or looked up, a kube configuration under HOME and the root folder of the host as a volume
when: Gives the checks of ST-STD-LOCAL-R01-T02 (workstationFaults and commandFaults) one planted test file at a time: sh -c with docker run --privileged; docker run -v /:/host; sh -c with podman run -v /:/host; exec.Command of a variable and of a constant that hold kubectl and /usr/local/bin/oc; exec.LookPath of kubectl; a read of $HOME/.kube/config and of the .docker folder under os.Getenv("HOME"); a shell that reads $HOME/.kube/config; and two controls, a volume of a temporary folder and a variable that holds go. Then it gives the line checks a planted file of Assuring's own checks with a pattern of regexp.MustCompile that holds --cap-add, a line with --cap-add that ends with the comment // regexp.MustCompile(, and one that ends with the old plant mark.
then: Expects a fault for each plant and none for the two controls. Expects the two lines that end with a comment to be read and found, and the pattern of regexp.MustCompile not to be read.
notes: A test of the test (security review of PR #504, the R01 line that was there before #504): proved by the subtest of this ID of TestLocalChecks; not a proof of the rule by itself, as the tree at HEAD holds none of the forms. Fails on the checks of main b019f7767 (fu-51): each plant gives no fault. Security review of PR #10, L3 (fu-51): the plant mark is gone, and in Assuring's own files only a line that holds a string literal of the pattern of a call of regexp.MustCompile, as go/parser finds it, is not read; the plants of this file are written in two pieces so that the scan of the tree does not read them. Mutation caught: the substring rules of before (the two lines are not read: 'find [], want the two marked lines').

title: Each test file belongs to one suite that one documented command runs
when: Reads the documented list of suite commands (the builder names the file and records it as tooling) and each test file that a test record names or that the config's test globs match (**/*_test.go, scripts/test_*.py).
then: Expects each suite in the list to have exactly one command, and each test file to belong to exactly one suite. Names each test file that no suite runs, and each suite with no command or with two.
notes: Not automated yet. Product-wide, so that a test file that no domain owns is also caught. Read the test globs from lathe.config.json, not from a copy, so a new kind of test file is also caught.

title: Each test file of the product belongs to one documented suite
when: Reads each file that an automated test record of the product names, and finds its suite: go test ./... of the Go module that holds it, or scripts/run-python-tests.py for scripts/test_*.py; a test file under testdata belongs to the suite of a Go test that names it.
then: Expects README.md to document go test ./..., scripts/run-python-tests.py to be in the tree, and each test file to belong to exactly one suite. Names each test file that no suite runs.
notes: Product-wide: it runs the check of ST-PAT-LOCAL-TEST-R02 on every automated test record of the product. Not automated yet: 13 test files fail or skip without STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN, which README.md does not name (review of PR #502, L4). Files: internal/compiler/database_access_integration_test.go internal/compiler/relationship_outbox_test.go internal/compiler/revocation_wiring_test.go internal/compiler/runtime_example_test.go internal/compiler/runtime_grpc_test.go internal/compiler/runtime_wiring_test.go internal/generator/browserbackend/testdata/application/socket_test.go internal/generator/command/service_test.go internal/generator/idempotency/emitted_test.go internal/generator/oidcauth/runtime_test.go internal/generator/restapi/runtime_data_test.go internal/generator/tenancy/generator_test.go internal/generator/worker/service_test.go .

title: The check of R02 counts a set of a variable only in the module of the test that sets it, and finds a read through a constant, a wrapper, a helper and an unlisted copy variable
when: Gives the check of the environment of ST-STD-LOCAL-R02-T02 (undocumentedEnvironment) a planted tree of two Go modules: the module other sets STEGO_PLANT_OTHER and STEGO_PLANT_SAME for a child process and reads STEGO_PLANT_SAME with a skip; the root module reads STEGO_PLANT_OTHER, reads STEGO_PLANT_CONSTANT through a constant, STEGO_PLANT_WRAPPED through a wrapper need(t, name) that skips, STEGO_PLANT_HELPER through a helper that returns the read, STEGO_PLANT_DUMP and STEGO_CRUD_DUMP directly, and STEGO_PLANT_DOCUMENTED, which the section of README.md names, each with a skip. The module other also has names.go, which gives the name key to STEGO_PLANT_COLLIDE, and the root module sets key, which there holds HOME, for a child process, and reads STEGO_PLANT_COLLIDE with a skip.
then: Expects faults for STEGO_PLANT_COLLIDE, STEGO_PLANT_CONSTANT, STEGO_PLANT_DUMP, STEGO_PLANT_HELPER, STEGO_PLANT_OTHER and STEGO_PLANT_WRAPPED only: the set of another module does not count, a name ending in _DUMP is not an opt-in unless the list names it, and the same-module set, the listed copy variable and the documented variable give none.
notes: A test of the test (security review of PR #504, L2 and N3): proved by the subtest of this ID of TestLocalChecks; not a proof of the rule by itself. Fails on the check of main b019f7767 (fu-51): it finds none of the five. Security review of PR #10, L2 (fu-51): a name is resolved in the package (folder) of the file that uses it, or, qualified, in the package that the file imports; before, names were keyed tree-wide, so a set of key in one module counted for a key of another. Mutation caught: names resolved tree-wide (STEGO_PLANT_COLLIDE is not found).

title: No obligation is proved only by a test that needs a real outside system
when: Reads the spec at the commit under test with the pinned Lathe and lists each test record that is external, or whose given, when, notes or test data set names an outside system: a hosted CI provider, Konflux, Argo CD, an OCI registry, an identity provider or a signer. For each, reads the other tests of the same obligation.
then: Expects each obligation that such a test proves to have at least one other test that runs against a local stand-in of that system, and names each obligation whose only tests need the real system.
notes: Not automated yet. Product-wide. The stand-ins are a local OCI registry (the TLS registry fixture, scripts/registry-fixture.go), PostgreSQL in a local container, a fake of the hosted CI provider's API, Konflux and Argo CD that keeps their contract, a fixture signer that the test trusts in place of the provider's signer, and a kind cluster only where a real Kubernetes API is the thing under test.

title: An inner go command does not take a module that only the shared module cache holds
when: Plants the module example.com/lib v1.0.0, which no sum database checked, in a module cache that GOMODCACHE names, as another tool fills the shared cache, and runs go mod tidy with localtest.GoEnv in a module that imports it and has no go.sum line for it.
then: Expects the tidy to fail and go.sum to name no planted module: GoEnv takes the module cache of localtest in place of the shared one.
notes: Fix of finding M1 of the security review of PR #510 (CWE-494). The reviewer's probe1 module, run against the old settings (the shared cache as proxy with GOSUMDB=off), was taken; against the cache of localtest it is refused.

title: A module that only the cache of localtest holds, with no checked go.sum line, fails the check of go.sum
when: Plants example.com/lib v1.0.0 straight into the module cache of localtest, past its fill and checks, runs go mod tidy with localtest.GoEnv in a module that imports it, and runs localtest.SumsChecked on the module.
then: Expects the tidy to take the module and the check to refuse it, naming example.com/lib v1.0.0, so a module in the cache that no checked go.sum names cannot pass.
notes: The second layer of the fix of M1: the union of the go.sum files of testdata/modules, testdata/modules-other, the root module and registry/runtime is the list of checked lines.

title: The module cache of localtest is neither the shared GOMODCACHE nor in the temporary folder, and the inner settings reach no host
when: Reads the module cache of localtest after its fill and the environment that GoEnv gives.
then: Expects the cache to be outside the GOMODCACHE of the go command and outside the temporary folder, and GoEnv to set its own GOMODCACHE, GOSUMDB=off, GONOPROXY=none, GONOSUMDB=none, GOINSECURE=, GOVCS=*:off, GOAUTH=off and GOENV=off.
notes: Findings M1 and L1 of the security review of PR #510.

title: When the module cache of localtest cannot be made, GoEnv gives no shared cache and a tidy of a planted module fails
when: Runs the test binary again, as a child, with STEGO_TEST_RUNS in its shared module cache and then in the temporary folder, so cacheFolder refuses the cache of localtest, with GOPATH/pkg/mod holding the planted module example.com/lib v1.0.0 and GOMODCACHE empty. The child runs go mod tidy with GoEnv in a module that imports the planted one.
then: Expects GoEnv to give an empty module cache of its own and GOPROXY=off, never an empty GOMODCACHE or the shared one, and the tidy to fail with no planted line in go.sum.
notes: Fix of finding L4 of the confirmation review of PR #510 (CWE-636). Shown to fail without the fix: with the fallback taken out, the tidy of the planted module succeeds. Packages whose tests run GoEnv call localtest.MainModules in TestMain, which runs no test when the cache cannot be used.

title: Each local service that a suite starts is pinned by digest or by exact version and checksum
when: Scans every suite file, test helper, test data set and fixture script for each local service it starts: a container image, a downloaded binary, a Go SDK or a tool.
then: Expects each to be named by a sha256 digest, or by an exact version with a checksum that the suite checks before use, and to be started by the test or its suite. Names each that is named by a tag such as latest, by a version range, or with no checksum, and each that a test expects to be running already.
notes: Not automated yet. Product-wide. A service that a test expects to find running, such as a database on a fixed port, is a fault even when it is pinned, because the suite does not start it.

title: Each container that a test of the product starts is pinned by digest
when: Reads each file that an automated test record of the product names and that starts a container, and lists each image that it names as the image of a container; then scans each file for a connection to a service at a fixed local port.
then: Expects each image to be pinned by a whole sha256 digest, and no test to expect a service that runs already at a fixed address. Names each image and line that breaks this.
notes: Product-wide: it runs the check of ST-PAT-LOCAL-TEST-R04 on every automated test record of the product. Not automated yet: on main, test files in internal/compiler, internal/generator and cmd/stego read STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN or STEGO_TEST_SPICEDB_ENDPOINT and fail or skip without it, and no harness of their package starts the server (review of PR #502, M3). They need a harness such as pgtest of the runtime module; then the subtest comes back.

title: A run of every suite leaves no file, container or process outside its temporary folder
when: Runs each suite command of the documented list with HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_DATA_HOME, XDG_STATE_HOME and TMPDIR each set to a new empty folder, and XDG_CACHE_HOME set to the cache of pinned downloads. Lists the user's files, containers, volumes, networks and processes before and after the run.
then: Expects no file outside TMPDIR to be new or changed, apart from the outcomes file that the command names and new entries of the cache that are keyed by digest. Expects no container, volume, network or process that the run started to be left. Names each one that is.
notes: Not automated yet. Product-wide. List the whole test folder, the user's containers (podman ps -a), volumes and networks, so that state left in an unexpected place is caught; ST-DLV-A4-SR01-T03 does the same for stego apply and stego delivery check.

title: A container of an image with no time limit is removed when the tests end and when the test binary is killed
when: Takes a container through Reap and a network through ReapNetwork with a tool that records its calls, and calls remove, as Main does when the tests end; then starts the reaper of a second container, reads its process group, checks the tool, closes the write end of the pipe of the reaper, as the end of the test binary on any path does, and waits for the call of the tool; then does the same for a network.
then: Expects remove to call the tool with rm --force and the container and then with network rm and the network, and both reapers to end with no call of their own; the second reaper in a process group of its own and no call of the tool while the pipe is open; then the call rm --force of the second container, and network rm of the network.
notes: Level: unit. The test is TestReap in registry/runtime/internal/pgtest/pgtest_test.go; the runtime-library workflow runs it (go test ./... of registry/runtime), but the proof run does not run the runtime module, so the gate cannot hold an outcome for it and the record stays not automated yet until the proof run takes registry/runtime. The SpiceDB image holds no timeout program, so the harnesses of the runtime module that start it (authz, query, service) give each container to pgtest.Reap; four stego-service-spicedb containers had run for 2 to 6 days (followups, 2026-11-17). The test waits for the reaper with no bound of its own: -test.timeout bounds it. The reaper reads a pipe whose write end only the test binary holds, so it watches no PID and a reused PID keeps no reaper alive; it runs in a process group of its own (Setpgid), so a kill of the group of the binary does not take it; Main tells it done after the removal, so it does not outlive a clean exit; ReapNetwork reaps a network of a harness after its containers (security review of PR #417, L1). A removal that fails leaves the reaper, which removes the object when the binary ends (security review of PR #429, L3).

title: No test of the product leaves a container or a file outside a temporary folder
when: Reads each file that an automated test record of the product names, and scans it for a write in the user's home folder or under a fixed folder of the host, and for a container that it starts and does not remove.
then: Expects none. Names each file and line that writes outside a temporary folder, and each file that starts a container that it does not remove when the test ends.
notes: Product-wide: it runs the check of ST-PAT-LOCAL-TEST-R05 on every automated test record of the product. This scan proves only part of the rule, so it is not counted as proof (review of PR #504, M7): it sees writes and containers that the code names, not what a run leaves behind. ST-STD-LOCAL-R05-T01, a run of every suite with fresh folders, proves the rest.

title: The walkthrough copy guard refuses a project link that resolves out of the project folder, does not resolve, or leaves the copy
when: Gives sameProjectInCopy, the guard that runs before a test copies the shared walkthrough build, three project folders in a temporary folder: one where deep/b links to .. and deep/a links to b/../outside, a file beside the project folder; one with a link to a missing file; and one whose links resolve in the folder through other links. Then copies two more folders beside them, each with a link that climbs out of the folder and back in by its base name: ../../project/inside, and b/../project/inside where b links to ..; and checks each link of each copy.
then: Expects the guard to refuse the first folder because the link resolves out of the folder, to refuse the second because the link does not resolve, and to accept the third. Expects both copies to be refused, because a link of the copy resolves out of the copy.
notes: Follow-up of the security review of PR #507, L1: the guard compared the text of a link target, and filepath.Join folded b/.. before b was resolved. Mutation caught: the old lexical check with filepath.Rel on the joined target. Security review of PR #511, L3: a link that climbs out and back in by the base name resolves in the folder, so only the check of the copy finds it. Mutation caught: no check of the links of the copy.

title: Each obligation that a cluster or volume test proves also has a test that runs on a workstation
when: Reads the spec at the commit under test with the pinned Lathe and lists each obligation with its tests, and the size, level and notes of each test.
then: Expects each obligation with a test of size volume or worst case, or a test whose notes or test data set need a shared cluster, also to have a test that runs on a workstation. Names each obligation whose only proof needs a cluster.
notes: Not automated yet. Product-wide. AGENTS.md keeps performance and stress tests off the workstation, so this rule asks for a second test, not for a change of those tests.

title: Each obligation with a cluster or volume test also has a test that runs on a workstation
when: Reads the automated test records of the product with their size, level, given, when, then and notes, by the obligation that each proves.
then: Expects each obligation whose automated tests need a shared cluster, or are of size volume or worst case at level service, system or browser, also to have an automated test that is neither. Names each obligation whose only proof needs a cluster.
notes: Product-wide: it runs the checks of the tests of ST-PAT-LOCAL-TEST on every automated test record of the product at once, also those that sit under no domain, such as the tests of a shared generator library. It reads the records in the pinned lathe check --json and the files they name at HEAD, before any run. A line that compiles a regular expression is not read, so a check can name the text that it looks for. ST-STD-LOCAL-R0x-T01, which runs every suite, stays the product-wide run.

title: No test record or measure expects debug-hatch output
when: Reads every test record, output contract and business outcome measure in data/ at the commit under test, and the observations.json and test files of the example services.
then: Expects no record about a generated service's signals whose expected result reads the output of log or log/slog or a line on standard error as its evidence, other than an expectation that standard error stays empty or that a text is absent, and no test file of an example service that asserts on standard error; the diagnostics of a command-line program, such as ST-SUP-RC04-OC30-T01, are not counted.
notes: Not automated yet: the probe runtime and its rules are not built yet. Planned file internal/assure/observability_standard_test.go. Owner decision of 2026-11-06: a declared domain probe is the only sanctioned path for a fill to emit logs or domain signals; log and log/slog stay allowed as a debug hatch only.

title: Every local start of a generated service sets the console sink
when: Reads the local test helpers that start a generated service (ST-PAT-LOCAL-TEST) and the documented local run steps at the commit under test.
then: Expects each one to set STEGO_PROBE_CONSOLE to json or logfmt.
notes: Not automated yet: the probe runtime and its rules are not built yet. Planned file internal/assure/observability_standard_test.go. Owner decision of 2026-11-06: a declared domain probe is the only sanctioned path for a fill to emit logs or domain signals; log and log/slog stay allowed as a debug hatch only.

title: No Kubernetes base or GitOps object that stego apply writes for an example sets the console sink
when: Reads each file under deploy/base, deploy/components and deploy/argocd of each example at HEAD, whatever its extension. Then builds stego from the tree at HEAD in a temporary folder, runs stego apply on a copy of each example with a delivery stanza for Argo CD, and reads each file that apply writes under the same folders.
then: Expects at least one file of the base, at least one generated file of deploy/argocd, and no file to name STEGO_PROBE_CONSOLE. Names each file that does.
notes: No example states a delivery stanza, so the committed files hold no GitOps object; the fresh generation adds one, and the test fails when it reads no file of deploy/argocd (review of PR #504, M3). A file of any extension is read, so a .env file that a configMapGenerator loads is read too. The platform requirements list names every variable for an overlay and is not read. delivery.WriteBase (ST-DLV-CMD03-H) leaves the variable out.

title: The runtime library registers and discovers nothing by name, struct tag or init
when: Parses each Go file of registry/runtime that is not a test file at HEAD, and reads its imports, its init functions, its reads of a struct tag, its uses of the registries and settings of the process, and the left side of each assignment.
then: Expects no import of plugin or expvar, no dot import, no read of a struct tag, no use of a registry or a setting of the process, no assignment to a variable of another package, and each init to be one of two forms: one call of Register of an internal package of the runtime module, or one loop that fills a map from a string constant. Names each file that breaks this.
notes: The two forms of init register nothing by name: the first gives an internal package a setter of the registering package's own type (authzclock, oteldeadline, txhold); the second fills the reserved words of PostgreSQL. Each setting of the whole process (flag outside a FlagSet, slog.SetDefault, slog.Default, log.Default, http.DefaultTransport, time.Local, sql.Register, gob.Register, the providers and the logger of OpenTelemetry, os.Setenv, os.Chdir, os.Umask, mime.AddExtensionType, signal.Notify, runtime/debug settings) fails the test unless the test lists it by file with its reason: service.UseJSONLog, which the generated code calls; a read of GOMAXPROCS with the literal argument 0, and of the default resolver, which change nothing (review of PR #504, M4, N2 and N4). The test harnesses pgtest and kafkatest are tooling and are not read. Not proved by this scan: the second clause, that the library calls into a service only through a value that the service's own code passed it.

title: No file of the runtime library imports reflect or unsafe
when: Parses each Go file of registry/runtime that is not a test file at HEAD, and reads its imports.
then: Expects no import of reflect or unsafe. Names each file that imports one.

title: Every archetype of the common registry pins the one runtime module of the registry, at the checksum of its folder
when: Loads the common registry of the checkout, reads the module path of registry/runtime/go.mod, and computes the go.sum hash of the module zip of registry/runtime at the version that the archetypes pin.
then: Expects the module path github.com/910-software-solutions/stego/registry/runtime, the same pin in every archetype, with that module path and that hash, and a LICENSE in registry/runtime that is the repository's LICENSE. Expects a failure that names the new hash and the archetype files to change, when registry/runtime changes and the pin does not.
notes: Proved by TestRuntimeReleasedWithTheCommonRegistry; its subtest carries this ID. The tag registry/runtime/<version> at the same tree gives the same zip, because the module folder holds its own LICENSE: the Go module proxy adds the repository's LICENSE to a module in a subfolder that has none. So the pin is the checksum of the release, before and after the tag. A change of registry/runtime is a new runtime version: the archetypes then get a new runtime.version and runtime.sum, and a new archetype version (ST-SUP-INV10). Mutation check: the test fails when the sum of one archetype changes, or when a file of registry/runtime changes.

title: A generated service that imports a runtime package resolves the pin from the common registry with no network, builds with the pinned Go and runs
when: With a common registry in a temporary folder that holds a copy of registry/runtime and an archetype with the pin of the shipped archetypes, a service whose one component emits a background task that allocates 10.00 USD in three with github.com/910-software-solutions/stego/registry/runtime/money is applied; module resolution (stego deps) runs with a private module cache and only local module proxies; the service is built with the pinned Go and the proxy off, and run; then it is built again with the work file of scripts/runtime-workspace.sh and an empty module cache, and run.
then: Expects go.mod to require only the pin, with no replace directive, go.sum to hold the pin's hash and the hash of its go.mod, no work file in the project and no drift. Expects each run to print allocated 334 USD 333 USD 333 USD and to stop cleanly on SIGTERM, and the workspace build to put no runtime version in the module cache.
notes: Proved by TestRuntimePinBuildsWithNoNetwork; its subtest carries this ID. It needs the Go SDK that STEGO pins: STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO names its bin/go, else the SDK that runs the test, and it fails on another version. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): Generating stages the runtime folder of the common registry as a file module proxy when the folder's zip has the pinned hash, and puts it before the configured proxies; the test sets GOPROXY to that proxy and the download cache of the machine's module cache, then off, and the sum database off, so no command reaches github.com or any other host. The third-party modules that the runtime library requires must be in the machine's module cache, as they are after a test of registry/runtime. Before the first tag registry/runtime/<version> (ST-DIS-UC11-R06), stego build download cannot fetch the pin from the public proxy (see the builder notes).

title: The local runtime proxy serves only the bytes of the zip whose sum the pin holds
when: The local runtime proxy is staged three times from a runtime folder in a temporary folder: with the pin at the sum of the folder's module zip, with a pin at another sum, and from a folder whose go.mod is a symbolic link to a go.mod outside it, with the pin at the sum of that folder's zip.
then: Expects, for the pinned folder, a proxy whose .mod file is the go.mod of the zip and a staged go.sum that holds its hash; for the other sum, no proxy and no proxy folder; and for the linked go.mod, a refusal that the zip holds no go.mod, with no proxy and no proxy folder.
notes: Security re-review of PR #400: L1 (the served go.mod and its hash come from the zip whose sum the pin holds, not from a second read of the folder) and L3 (a forged pin sum gives no local proxy). Security review of PR #436, L2: each error removes the partial proxy folder, so a caller that keeps the stage can stage it again. Mutation caught: the cleanup on error removed (the proxy folder stayed).

title: The runtime archive hashes the zip and reads its go.mod from the one copy that it writes
when: Writes the runtime archive of a runtime folder in a temporary folder, then makes the archive of the bytes of the written zip, of a zip with two go.mod entries and of a zip with no go.mod.
then: Expects the sum of the archive to be the hash of the written zip, its go.mod the one of the folder, the archive of the written bytes the same, and a refusal of the zip with two go.mod entries and of the zip with no go.mod.
notes: Security review of PR #436: L1 (the archive made the zip, hashed it by path and then opened it again by path to read go.mod, so a process of the same user could change the zip between the two reads; it now makes the zip in memory and hashes and reads those bytes before it writes them) and I1 (a zip with two go.mod entries is refused, not read at its first one). Mutation caught: the second go.mod entry skipped (the zip with two go.mod entries passed).

title: The runtime archive refuses a folder whose module zip is larger than its limit
when: Writes the runtime archive of a runtime folder in a temporary folder that holds 8 KiB of random bytes, with the limit of 64 MiB, then with a limit of the size of that zip, then with a limit one byte less; then writes 6, 5, 4 and 1 bytes to a capped buffer of 10 bytes.
then: Expects the limit MaxRuntimeArchive to be 64 MiB, the zip to be written with the limit of 64 MiB and with the limit of its size, and ErrRuntimeArchiveSize and no zip file with the limit one byte less; and a capped buffer with no ReadFrom and no WriteString method, the writes of 6 and 4 bytes taken, the writes of 5 and 1 bytes refused with ErrRuntimeArchiveSize, and 10 bytes in a capacity of 10.
notes: Security review of PR #442, L2: the archive made the zip in memory with only the limit of 500 MiB of the module zip package, so a wrong registry folder could make it hold about 1 GiB. Security review of PR #445, I-3: the buffer embedded bytes.Buffer, whose ReadFrom and WriteString skip the cap and whose doubling can take twice the limit; now its bytes are a named field of a fixed capacity. Mutation caught: the buffer takes a write past its limit (the zip one byte larger than its limit was written); the buffer that embeds bytes.Buffer (it has ReadFrom and WriteString). Not caught: WriteRuntimeArchive with a limit other than MaxRuntimeArchive, as a folder of 64 MiB is too large for a unit test.

title: Only the connector package of the runtime library imports a database driver, and no exported function takes a driver's transaction
when: Parses each Go file of registry/runtime that is not a test file at HEAD, and reads its imports and the parameters of its exported functions.
then: Expects no import of a database driver (pgx, lib/pq, a MySQL or SQLite driver) outside registry/runtime/pgconn, except the imports that the test lists by file as not closed yet, and no exported function that takes the transaction type of a driver. Names each other import and each such function. Also expects each listed file to be in the runtime library and to import each import that the test lists for it; for a listed entry that the tree no longer has, it says that the gap closed and that the entry must be removed.
notes: This scan proves only the import part of the rule, so it is not counted as proof (review of PR #504, M7). Not proved: that the tests reach PostgreSQL through pgx's database/sql driver, and that the listener refuses a pooled DSN (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R06-T02). The listed imports are the gap that ST-SUP-RP04-LF08 (registry/runtime/pgconn/connect.go, not written yet) closes.

title: Only the connector package imports a driver, and the listener refuses a pooled DSN
when: Reads the imports of every non-test file of the runtime module, and opens the outbox Listener of the connector package with a DSN that names a transaction-mode pooler and with a direct DSN.
then: Expects a database driver imported only by files of github.com/910-software-solutions/stego/registry/runtime/pgconn, the pooled DSN refused at start with an error that names the setting and no secret, and the direct DSN accepted.
notes: Planned as a check of the code-standard tests in internal/assure, beside ST-STD-RUNTIME-R06-T01, and a unit test in registry/runtime/pgconn/listen_test.go. Today the tenant package imports pgx outside its tests; the code change moves that code to pgconn. Review of PR #143 (outbox runtime).

title: The compiler contains a generator for every component the registry ships
when: Lists the components in registry/components and the generators the compiler build holds.
then: Expects each component to have a generator, and each generator to have a component.

title: Qualification fails when the signed artifact run holds a second artifact
when: Qualifies a release whose signed artifact run also holds a separate generator artifact.
then: Expects qualification to fail on an unknown artifact, so a release ships one compiler.

title: A component with no generator in the compiler build stops compilation before anything is written
when: Compiles a service whose component has no generator, a nil generator or a typed nil generator.
then: Expects a validation error and no plan, with no output, go.mod or .stego written; the compiler looks for no generator elsewhere.

title: No compiler source imports the plugin package
when: Parses the imports of every non-test Go source under cmd and internal, outside testdata.
then: Expects no import of Go's plugin package, so the compiler cannot load code at run time.
notes: This shows the compiler cannot load code. It does not show that the compiler downloads or runs no generator code by other means.

title: The Argo CD adapter writes files and calls no API, runs no command and reads no credential
when: Parses each Go file that is not a test file in the package of the adapter ST-INT03-AD (internal/delivery) at HEAD, and reads its imports and each reference to a function of package os, io/ioutil and net.
then: Expects each import to be on the allow list of the test (the standard library's text, encoding, data and error packages, net/url, net, the YAML package and the application build), no dot import, from net only SplitHostPort, from internal/appbuild only GoVersion, BuildFlags and BuildEnvironment, and no reference, as a call or as a value, to a function that reads the environment or a file (os.Getenv, os.LookupEnv, os.Environ, os.ExpandEnv, os.Expand, os.ReadFile, os.Open, os.ReadDir, os.DirFS and the like). Expects at least two files to be read. Names each file that breaks this.
notes: The adapter's file can call each function of its package, so the test reads the whole package and not the adapter's file only (review of PR #504, M2). net and internal/appbuild can also reach the network or run a command (appbuild.Download, net.ListenTCP), so the test admits by name only the parts of them that the package uses (review of PR #504, N1).

title: The tenant setting is set only transaction-local, with set_config and true
when: Reads the store code at HEAD: the Go files that are not test files, the templates of generated Go and the SQL files of registry/runtime and internal/generator, outside testdata. Lists each set_config of app.tenant, reads its third argument after the value with balanced brackets, and lists each SET of app.tenant.
then: Expects at least one set_config of app.tenant, each with true as its third argument, and no SET of app.tenant. Names each that breaks this.
notes: This scan proves only part of the rule, so it is not counted as proof (review of PR #504, M7). The record stays not automated yet until a test proves the rest. Not proved: that the tenant is set at the start of every transaction of the generated store code; the scan sees how it is set, not where. ST-STD-TXN-R02-T02 proves the scan on good and bad forms.

title: The scan of the tenant setting tells a transaction-local set from a session set
when: Gives the scan of ST-STD-TXN-R02-T01 a table of statements: set_config with true, with false after a value with brackets and commas, across lines, and a SET or SET LOCAL of app.tenant.
then: Expects a fault for each session set and each SET, and none for a transaction-local set.
notes: A test of the test (review of PR #504, M1); it proves no part of the rule by itself, so it is not automated yet as a proof of the rule. Security review of PR #504, L3 (fu-51): the scan also finds set_config with a space before its parenthesis and in upper case; the subtest has these plants.

title: Each role or user that STEGO creates is NOBYPASSRLS and NOSUPERUSER
when: Reads the store code at HEAD as ST-STD-TXN-R02-T01 does, and lists each CREATE ROLE and CREATE USER with its attributes, also those that a format string takes from one flags variable, and each ALTER ROLE or ALTER USER.
then: Expects at least one, each with NOSUPERUSER and NOBYPASSRLS, and no ALTER that gives SUPERUSER or BYPASSRLS. Names each that breaks this.
notes: This scan proves only part of the rule, so it is not counted as proof (review of PR #504, M7). The record stays not automated yet until a test proves the rest. Not proved: that the runtime role owns no table, holds only the privileges that the generated code uses, and that migrations run as the owner in a separate job. checkRuntimeRole of the tenant runtime (ST-SUP-RP04-LC06) holds them at run time.

title: The scan of roles finds a role or a user with SUPERUSER or BYPASSRLS
when: Gives the scan of ST-STD-TXN-R03-T01 a table of CREATE ROLE, CREATE USER and ALTER ROLE statements.
then: Expects a fault for each role or user with no NOSUPERUSER or no NOBYPASSRLS, and each ALTER that gives one.
notes: A test of the test (review of PR #504, M3); not a proof of the rule by itself. Security review of PR #504, L3 (fu-51): the scan also finds a grant of a role with the privileges of a superuser, such as GRANT postgres TO and rds_superuser; a grant of another role or of a table named postgres gives none.

title: No store code grants UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE or ALL on the audit table, and triggers reject them
when: Reads the store code at HEAD as ST-STD-TXN-R02-T01 does, and lists each GRANT whose target names the audit events table in any form ({events}, audit_event, EventsTable); then reads the triggers and the reject function in registry/runtime/audit/jobs.go.
then: Expects at least one grant on the table, none of UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE or ALL, the row and statement triggers on the table and on each partition, and the function that raises an exception.
notes: This scan proves only part of the rule, so it is not counted as proof (review of PR #504, M7). The record stays not automated yet until a test proves the rest. Not proved: that every audit row is enqueued in the outbox for the audit sink, keyed by the audit event id; the library contract tests of ST-SUP-RP05 hold it on a database.

title: The scan of audit grants finds a write grant on the audit table in any form of its name
when: Gives the scan of ST-STD-TXN-R06-T01 a table of grants on the audit table and on other tables.
then: Expects a fault for each grant of UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE or ALL on the audit table, and none for SELECT, INSERT or another table.
notes: A test of the test (review of PR #504, M5); not a proof of the rule by itself. Security review of PR #504, L3 (fu-51): the scan also finds a write grant on ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA of an audit schema and on stego_audit_sink.entries, also in the Go joins of auditsink/table.go; a second subtest of this ID holds the joins.

title: No code of the money and ledger runtime or of the ledger generator holds an amount as a float
when: Reads the store code of registry/runtime/money, registry/runtime/ledger and internal/generator/ledger at HEAD, in Go and in SQL text.
then: Expects no float32, float64, math/big or ParseFloat, and no double precision, real or float in SQL. Names each that breaks this.
notes: This scan proves only part of the rule, so it is not counted as proof (review of PR #504, M7). The record stays not automated yet until a test proves the rest. Not proved: an ISO 4217 currency, a float refused at checking of the declaration, and one currency per ledger; the library contract tests of ST-SUP-RP08 and the declaration checks hold them.

title: The scan of money finds a float in Go and in SQL
when: Gives the scan of ST-STD-TXN-R12-T01 a table of Go and SQL text.
then: Expects a fault for each float, and none for an integer amount or a comment.
notes: A test of the test (review of PR #504, M6); not a proof of the rule by itself.

title: Each claim of rows in the runtime library and the generators skips locked rows and takes no session lock
when: Reads the store code at HEAD as ST-STD-TXN-R02-T01 does, as whole text across lines and Go string joins, and lists each claim of a batch of rows (LIMIT and then FOR UPDATE) and each session-scoped advisory lock.
then: Expects at least one claim, each with SKIP LOCKED apart from the listed paged row locks of the seal job, and no session lock apart from the listed files of the migration job and of provisioning.
notes: This scan proves only part of the rule, so it is not counted as proof (review of PR #504, M7). The record stays not automated yet until a test proves the rest. Not proved: that a handler is idempotent, or that an unknown outcome is reconciled or parked; the library contract tests of the outbox (ST-SUP-RP01) hold it.

title: The scan of claims finds a claim with no SKIP LOCKED across lines and Go string joins
when: Gives the scan of ST-STD-TXN-R14-T01 a table of claims and locks.
then: Expects a fault for each claim with no SKIP LOCKED and each session lock, and none for a claim with SKIP LOCKED or a lock of one row by its key.
notes: A test of the test (review of PR #504, M2); not a proof of the rule by itself. Security review of PR #504, L3 (fu-51): the scan also finds a row lock before the LIMIT, FETCH FIRST ... ROWS ONLY with a lock, FOR SHARE and FOR KEY SHARE, and pg_advisory_lock_shared and an upper-case lock; the subtest has these plants. Mutation: the one regular expression of main: the lock before the LIMIT and the shared and upper-case locks give no fault.

title: No statement of the runtime library or of a generated service names a table or a function of a schema manifest with no schema
when: Reads each Go file that is not a test file of the runtime library and of the generated code of each example, and each template of a generator, at the commit under test. It folds each string expression over the constants and string variables of its package and of each package of the tree that it imports, through more than one package, the migration of the key table that the owner runs included, over the local variables that are set once and over the unexported fields of a struct whose every value gives the same text; a package variable that its package sets again is unknown. It reads only the string literals of each .go.tmpl file, each other .sql and .tmpl file whole, and each action of a template as an argument, with the tables of the runtime manifests and of the schema manifest of each example. A text that starts with a statement word is searched in any case; in another text only the keywords in upper case count. It finds, across lines, each table after FROM, INTO, UPDATE, JOIN, TRUNCATE, LOCK TABLE, COPY, TABLE or USING, after a comma of a FROM list or in a regclass cast, that is not a common table expression of the text, and each function of the runtime after SELECT, FROM, PERFORM, CALL, a comma or a parenthesis, that has no schema; outside a .go.tmpl file also each table keyword followed by a format argument or another value with no dot after it, and each text that ends with a table keyword, other than FOR UPDATE, FOR SHARE, DO UPDATE, DISTINCT FROM and the roles of GRANT and REVOKE. Then it runs the same search on a probe tree with one file for each form.
